ruleName: Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions (Including Immovable Obstructions)
title: Playing a Ball from Steps
question: Sophie wants to play her ball as it lies from some steps, but David insists she must take relief. Sophie chooses to play the ball from the steps. What is the ruling?

choices.text: David receives the general penalty for giving advice.
Sophie must take a drop and gets a penalty if she does not.

explanation: There is no penalty for playing a ball as it lies on immovable obstructions such as steps. Relief is optional under Rule 16.1a.

juniorVersion.title: Can Sophie Hit Her Ball from the Steps?
juniorVersion.question: Sophie’s ball lands on some steps next to the path. She says she wants to hit it from there. David tells her she has to move it. Sophie decides to hit the ball from the steps. What happens?

choices.text: David gets a penalty for telling Sophie what to do.
Sophie must drop the ball somewhere else and gets a penalty if she doesn’t.

juniorVersion.explanation: Sophie is allowed to hit her ball from the steps if she wants to. She does not have to move it. There is no penalty for this.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: Something on the course that you can’t move, like steps or a big sign.
A choice to move your ball to a better spot when it is on something like steps or a path.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Let children try playing from different places like paths or steps. Show they do not have to move the ball if they don’t want to.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think they always have to move the ball off a path or steps.
Children may believe they get a penalty just for playing from the steps.
